newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korea Sewon to absorb Miwon.
newsitem.headline: S.Korea Sewon to absorb Miwon.

text.p: South Korean corn starch producer Sewon Co has decided to absorb its sister company Miwon Co to improve international competitiveness, the Securities Supervisory Board said on Thursday.
Every 100 common shares of Miwon will be exchanged into 20.59 new shares of Sewon and every 100 preferred shares into 21.71 new preferred shares, the statement said.
Sewon's common shares are now trading at 91,600 won, against Miwon's at 19,900 won, and Sewon's preferred shares 20005.KS are now at 24,200 won versus Miwon's at 5,340 won.
The absorption plan was subject to approval at the two companies' shareholders meetings on July 16 with an effective date of November 1, the statement said.
Miwon and the family of its chairman currently hold the largest single stake of 48.21 percent in Sewon, it said.
After the absorption, Sewon's paid-in capital would rise to 25.12 billion won from 14.83 billion won at present, the statement said.
Sewon posted a net profit of 16.61 billion won in 1996 on turnover of 286.66 billion won, while Miwon recorded 6.71 billion won profit on 625.43 billion won turnover, it said.
